svg.title: Trusting the installer on a fresh machine — The installer fixes its own gaps, and stays interactive even when piped
svg.text: Trusting the installer on a fresh machine
Scenario: The installer fixes its own gaps, and stays interactive even when piped
A bare machine sets itself up

g.text: Given a fresh machine has only sudo and curl, with the installer ready
to run
This machine has sudo and curl but no unzip — the tool the installer will have to add by
itself. The installer files are copied in but not started yet.
When the installer runs on the fresh machine with no one to answer its
questions
The installer starts and prints its title. Nothing on the machine has changed yet.
Then the installer installs the tool it was missing and tries again
task devsecops:init fails because unzip is missing, so the installer adds unzip with sudo
and runs again. The log is checked for the same story.
And the installer stops and explains how to link the project to GitLab
The installer stops on purpose: the project has no GitLab link yet, so it prints the exact
next step. If this message ever went missing, a new developer would be stuck.

text.tspan: No 'origin' remote configured. Add a GitLab remote, then re-run.

g.text: Given a developer follows the README and pipes the installer into bash
The empty copy, with the installer ready to run the documented way — piped into bash (the
output of one command fed straight into the next). Set up off-screen: the test user, the
tools, and the GitLab login.
When the installer still asks what to install, even when piped into
bash
Even when piped into bash, the installer still reaches its first question: it reads your
keystrokes through /dev/tty, so the documented one-line command still lets you answer.
Then the piped install finishes and opens the framework merge request
Answering through the pipe builds and finishes exactly like typing the command by hand. The
test also checks the API (the init-framework-devsecops branch and its open merge request
into main) and the finished line in the log.
